neighbours.label: the noun right after 'thin' (thin layer, thin ice, thin film), as against the same noun after another adjective
fire: The paint dries to a thin film on the metal.
A thin sheet of glass separates the two chambers.
Spread a thin coat of glue on both surfaces.
The mountain climbers struggled in the thin air.
The cell is surrounded by a thin membrane of lipids.
Cut the cucumber into thin slices for the salad.
Only a thin crust of snow remained on the path.
The novel has a thin plot but beautiful prose.
quiet: The paint dries to a hard film on the metal.
A heavy sheet of glass separates the two chambers.
Spread a second coat of glue on both surfaces.
The mountain climbers struggled in the cold air.
The cell is surrounded by a double membrane of lipids.
Cut the cucumber into round slices for the salad.
Only a hard crust of snow remained on the path.
The novel has a simple plot but beautiful prose.
